Dustin Swedelson|KENTUCKY OVER 4.5 WINS.summary: Swedelson finds a lot to like even allowing that Kentucky is a basketball school. His central observation is that the Wildcats scored 17 points or fewer six times in 2025 and still found five wins, so a modest offensive improvement should at least hold five and clear this total. That is why they turned to Will Stein: never a head coach before, but the man who ran an Oregon offense across three seasons that made Bo Nix a first-round pick, Dillon Gabriel a third-rounder, and turned Dante Moore from a UCLA cast-off into a potential top-five pick. Kenny Minchey is the next project.
Dustin Swedelson|KENTUCKY OVER 4.5 WINS.depends_on: coaching (Stein's quarterback development record); quarterback (Minchey); the low bar set by last year's five wins

Dustin Swedelson|NC STATE OVER 7.5 WINS.summary: Swedelson's case is Dave Doeren's consistency in year 16: he has failed to reach eight wins only once since 2020, and Swedelson says it may be neither pretty nor exciting but Doeren wins games. He acknowledges the offense that scored 30.2 points per game lost juice with Hollywood Smothers and all five leading pass catchers gone, but the reason he thinks eight wins is reachable is quarterback CJ Bailey returning for a third season and a second under coordinator Kurt Roper. He calls Bailey's decision to stay in Raleigh shocking given what the portal would have paid after 3,105 passing yards, 31 total touchdowns and nine interceptions.
Dustin Swedelson|NC STATE OVER 7.5 WINS.depends_on: coaching (Doeren's floor, Roper continuity); quarterback (Bailey's return); heavy losses at receiver

He walks the slate: Utah in week two, Georgia a week later, Tulsa on September 26 as a likely win but a dreaded lookahead with Texas A&M the following week, then a brutal close from Halloween — Missouri at home, at an improved Auburn, South Carolina, at Texas, and LSU. He cites Pick Six Previews: the average Big 12 team signed two four-star transfers over the past two recruiting periods, and Texas Tech signed 20.
